series.name: 7 things nobody tells you before your first time
series.label: Nobody tells you this · 5 of 7

beats.vo: You don't need to know what you're doing your first time.

overlay.text: You don't need to know what you're doing.

beats.visual_intent: One lamp glowing in a dark room. Single subject, high contrast. No people.

beats.vo: You need to pay attention to her. If she seems into it, stay with what's working.
beats.visual_intent: Tuning in, listening closely: a record player needle on vinyl, close up. No people.

beats.vo: If she goes quiet, still, pulls away, or seems unsure, slow down and check in. Body language gives you information. It doesn't replace asking.

overlay.text: Body language is information. Not a yes.

beats.visual_intent: Two empty chairs facing each other, warm low light, no people.

beats.vo: When your nerves drag you into your own head, bring your attention back to her.
beats.visual_intent: A busy, spinning mind: night traffic light trails or city lights blurring past. Motion, no people.

beats.vo: Number four is next: how to check in without killing the mood.
